topicName: Enterprise Policy Management, Organization-level Actions, and Templates
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Enterprise Policy Management, Organization-level Actions, and Templates in GitHub Actions"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Scaling GitHub Actions across a large enterprise requires centralized governance to ensure security, compliance, and consistency. This tutorial covers how to enforce policies at the enterprise level, manage actions across organizations, and use workflow templates to standardize deployments."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Enterprise-Level Policy Management"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Enterprise owners can control which actions are available to all organizations within the enterprise. This is crucial for preventing supply chain attacks by restricting the use of unverified third-party actions."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Navigate to your Enterprise account settings and select "Policies" followed by "Actions"."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Choose between allowing all actions, local actions only, or selecting specific allowed actions (including actions created by GitHub and verified creators)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure restrictions for public and private repositories independently."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Organization-Level Actions and Secrets"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below the enterprise level, organization administrators can share common secrets, variables, and custom actions across multiple repositories within the same organization, reducing duplication and maintenance overhead."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"name: Reusable Security Scan
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      environment:
        required: true
        type: string
jobs:
  scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run Enterprise Security Tool
        run: echo "Running security audit for environment ${{ inputs.environment }}""},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Utilizing Workflow Templates"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Enterprise and organization owners can create standardized workflow templates. When developers create a new repository or workflow, these templates ensure they follow best practices out of the box."},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To create an organization-level workflow template, create a repository named ".github" within your organization. Inside this repository, add workflow files to a folder named "workflow-templates/" along with corresponding metadata files."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"name: CI Pipeline Template
description: Standard CI pipeline enforcing company linting and testing standards
files:
  - workflow.yml
publish_settings:
  custom_properties:
    scope: enterprise-standard"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining enterprise action policies, reusable workflows, and standardized organization templates, platform engineering teams can establish a secure, scalable, and compliant CI/CD ecosystem across all repositories."}]
